title: Loading, empty, success, failure, offline UI states
learningObjectives: Explain loading, empty, success, failure, offline ui states and implement reliable browser event and network workflows.

understand.concept: Network interfaces should model loading, success with data, empty results, failure, and offline or stale-data conditions. Each state needs useful text and appropriate retry or recovery actions. navigator.onLine is only a hint, not proof that a request will succeed.
understand.whyItMatters: Explicit states prevent blank screens and misleading success messages. Cached data may help offline but should be labelled accurately when stale.
understand.analogy: A delivery tracker distinguishes preparing, delivered, nothing available, failed, and temporarily disconnected.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; JavaScript scheduling, HTTP semantics, and browser security follow platform standards.

explain.narrative: The helper maps known states to readable messages. Real handlers should set state based on actual request results.

examples.code: function stateMessage(state){return ({loading:'Loading…',empty:'No results.',success:'Loaded.',failure:'Could not load.',offline:'You appear offline.'})[state]??'Unknown state'}console.log(stateMessage('empty'));
examples.explanation: The helper maps known states to readable messages. Real handlers should set state based on actual request results.
examples.expectedOutput: Console or UI output demonstrates the concept; network examples require a configured endpoint.

practise.guidedTask: Build a list page with all five states. Test loss of connectivity during a request and recovery.
practise.independentTask: Build an asynchronous feature with explicit states, cancellation, and error handling. Document which failures are safe to retry.
hints: Separate HTTP errors from network and parsing errors.
Use bounded retries only for suitable operations.
Tie UI updates to the latest active request.

questions.prompt: Does navigator.onLine prove an API request will succeed?
questions.explanation: navigator.onLine is a connectivity hint; the actual request determines success.

questions.prompt: What is a reliable approach to network-driven UI?
options: Model loading, empty, success, failure, and cancellation states
Assume every fulfilled fetch means HTTP success
questions.answer: Model loading, empty, success, failure, and cancellation states
questions.explanation: Explicit states and bounded recovery make network interfaces predictable and safe.
